# `company.scheduled_holds`

Automatic memorized entries the scheduler leaves for a person: entered unattended only when one principal decided both their content and their schedule.

Database: `company`.

| Column | SQL type | Nullable | Default | Key | Indexes | References | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `occurrence_id` | VARCHAR(26) | no | — | primary key 1 | — | — | Memorized occurrence the scheduler would not enter unattended. |
| `reason` | VARCHAR(400) | no | — | — | — | — | Why it waits for a person: who memorized it and who scheduled it, a schedule set before the upgrade, or a catch-up window someone else widened. |
| `created_at` | VARCHAR(32) | no | — | — | — | — | UTC time the scheduler set it aside. |
| `catch_up_window` | INTEGER | yes | — | — | — | — | The catch-up window, in days, it was left for a person under; null when held for another reason. A later run enters it only if its author set the current window or every widening since. |
